correctness.rationale: Every edge vertex has squared norm 2. The projection-minimax lemma proves that the unique enclosing-ball center is the minimum-norm point in the edge polytope. Class masses \(t_j\) form the rank-two hypersimplex; Cauchy-Schwarz and strict convexity yield either uniform center or saturated largest class. Explicit dot products give every sphere contact and clearance. A sharp two-stage Cauchy-Schwarz lower bound has an attained feasible witness for each missing edge vertex. Strict equality in the convex residual triangle inequality classifies the entire farthest set, including low-dimensional and threshold cases. Actual standalone exact-rational checker: 258 profiles, 8704 edge contacts, 198 strict noncontacts, 3150 forbidden-vertex projections; separate numerical optimization 10 profiles. All-dimensional proof independent of finite tests.

value.rationale: Graph edge polytopes and rank-two matroid bases are canonical geometric objects, and exact outer sphere and Hausdorff approximation loss are natural and previously non-implied quantities. The threshold at the largest class comprising half the vertices delineates two global geometric phases: entire orbits of vertices can be deleted with a fixed positive Hausdorff defect but no outer-ball change, whereas a dominant class shrinks the outer ball and screens contacts. Explicit nearest points and equality sets strengthen this structural classification beyond a routine isolated calculation; no downstream theorem is presumed.
